newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PANTHERS SPOIL GRETZKY'S HOME DEBUT AS A RANGER.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-PANTHERS SPOIL GRETZKY'S HOME DEBUT AS A RANGER.

text.p: Wayne Gretzky's first game in front of his new home fans on Sunday was hardly a Great One.

The Florida Panthers, who held Gretzky to one assist, got two goals from Brian Skrudland, including the tie-breaker 6:20 into the third period, and Rob Niedermayer added a pair of goals as the Panthers spoiled the home opener for Gretzky's New York Rangers 5-2.
Skrudland's second goal of the game, a high wrist shot over Mike Richter's glove, came just 56 seconds after Pat Flatley's tally tied it 2-2.
Scott Mellanby converted a 3-on-1 with 2:57 remaining to make it 4-2 and Niedermayer's second goal, just 43 seconds later, capped the scoring.
Panthers goalie John Vanbiesbrouck, an ex-Ranger, made 34 saves, stopping all 17 shots he faced in the first period.

Trailing 2-0 on goals by Skrudland and Niedermayer, the Rangers got on the board with a power-play goal by Niklas Sundstrom, who deflected Bruce Driver's point shot past Vanbiesbrouck with 7:27 left in the second period. Gretzky assisted on the goal for his first point as a Ranger.
In St. Louis, Chris Chelios and Murray Craven had a goal and an assist apiece and Tony Amonte set up a pair of scores as the Chicago Blackhawks defeated the Blues 4-1.
After St. Louis took a 1-0 lead on a goal by Peter Zezel, the Blackhawks responded with four unanswered tallies.
Craven drew Chicago even when he took a pass from Amonte, who was stationed behind the net, and slid the puck under the pads of Blues goaltender Grant Fuhr.
James Black snapped the tie 54 seconds into the second period when he tipped home a slap shot by Chelios.
Chelios and Ethan Moreau added third-period goals for the Hawks, who won its season opener in Washington on Saturday.
Chicago goalie Jeff Hackett stopped 36-of-37 shots in his first start of the season while Fuhr turned aside 27 shots.

In Edmonton, Curtis Joseph stopped 35 shots, including 17 in the final period, for his sixth career shutout and Dean McAmmond and Rem Murray scored goals 93 seconds apart in the first-period as the Oilers blanked the Vancouver Canucks 2-0.
Joseph made six saves during a Vancouver power play early in the third period and stoned Pavel Bure on a breakaway with 3:30 remaining.
"The key was not letting them get many second shots," Joseph said. "We did an excellent job of clearing the puck and keeping their scorers away from the front of the net."
Corey Hirsch and Kirk McLean combined to stop 30 Oiler shots.
In Calgary, Rick Tabaracci stopped 19 shots and Chris O'Sullivan, James Patrick and German Titov each scored as the Flames blanked the Buffalo Sabres 3-0.
Tabaracci stopped four shots in the first, eight in the second and seven in the third for his ninth career shutout.

After a scoreless first period, and with Buffalo's Michael Grosek serving a slashing minor, Titov passed to O'Sullivan, a rookie defenceman, who one-timed a shot over Dominik Hasek's glove with just over six minutes left in the second period.
Patrick later wristed a blast over Hasek's left shoudler with 5:35 to go in the third, and Titov capped the scoring with an epmty-netter.
Hasek made 24 saves for the Sabres, who have managed just three goals in their first two games, both losses.
At Los Angeles, Viktor Kozlov's goal with four seconds remaining in overtime lifted the San Jose Sharks past the Los Angeles Kings, 7-6.
Kelly Hrudey, who made his return to Los Angeles after signing as a free-agent with San Jose in the off-season made 31 saves.
